title: Submitting patches: the essential guide to getting your changes upstream
author: The Linux kernel community
version: 2026-11-14; the address is the publisher's canonical page and was not fetched in this container, so the revision is named rather than read

record.source: One logical change per patch, no unrelated changes mixed in, and every patch builds so that a bisect names a single commit; the message states why the change is needed, and a series is reviewed patch by patch.
record.kept: The properties: a commit holds the whole of its change (atomic), every commit builds and passes (bisectable), and the message states its reason (self-explanatory).
record.rewritten: The mechanism. The kernel sends patches by mail, reviews a series on a list, and keeps each patch independently applicable; this repository lands one delivery commit through the host verbs, so the unit is the iteration and the series is the branch.
record.added: The blameable and no-noise properties, which the guide does not state, and the delivery-commit grain.
record.dropped: Signed-off-by and the certificate of origin, the cover letter, the mail client, and the maintainer hierarchy.
